result:
I approved WP0 in round 2; the review is in `orders/review-wp0-2.md`.

The gate is clean: no new test failures, ruff and mypy pass, and there is one migration head. All four code problems from round 1 are fixed, and the seven planned tests now exist.

Two points need action, though neither blocks this stage:
- **NOT NULL on `work_items.workflow_id` is left hanging.** The migration leaves the column nullable and says WP1 will make it NOT NULL, but the WP1 section of the plan never mentions it. The WP1 order needs to require a new migration that back-fills and then sets NOT NULL. It also needs `mark_work_item` to fill in the column, and a default workflow for teams created after this migration. Without that, new items get no workflow version.
- **Access grants go beyond the plan.** The migration grants DELETE on `work_items` and UPDATE on `work_item_history`, and `downgrade()` never removes them. That leaves the "history can't be edited" rule resting on a single database policy.

Two smaller test gaps are also noted:
- The seed and back-fill tests re-run copies of the SQL on fresh teams, so they don't prove that teams which already existed got a workflow.
- The cross-team test only checks that an outsider can't read another team's item, not that they can't change it or add history to it.
